account: A 57-year-old woman in Zurich, Switzerland, noticed in her Fitbit Alta HR application that her resting heart rate had risen persistently from about 55 to about 75 beats per minute over three months, alongside non-specific constitutional symptoms. Two months before she came to University Hospital Zurich, her general practitioner ordered a chest computed tomography (CT) scan that was read as normal, although it showed a mild thickening of the aortic wall. Her general practitioner then treated her for polymyalgia rheumatica, and she was referred to Zurich when her symptoms returned on a lower steroid dose. The elevated resting heart rate led her to seek advice at University Hospital Zurich. Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography with CT (FDG-PET/CT) showed inflammation of the aorta and both subclavian and axillary arteries, consistent with large vessel vasculitis. Prednisone 50 mg daily rapidly improved her symptoms and normalized her resting heart rate within ten days. Tocilizumab was introduced as a steroid-sparing treatment two weeks later. Inflammatory markers normalized within two weeks. Four weeks after treatment began she reported that she was well, with a normal resting heart rate. A case report appeared in BMJ Case Reports on 28 February 2022, and it does not report the event dates.
